summary:
The Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-41, H.R. 7454, enacted March 8, 2024) is a short-term reauthorization measure that extends expiring Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) program authorities and Airport and Airway Trust Fund financing provisions through, in most cases, May 10 or May 11, 2024, primarily by amending title 49, United States Code, and the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. The bill operates almost exclusively through date-substitution amendments and revised interim authorization figures for the period beginning October 1, 2023.

Title I addresses FAA programs. Section 101 amends 49 U.S.C. 48103(a) to authorize $2,041,120,218 for the airport improvement program (AIP) through May 10, 2024; obligation authority runs through September 30, 2024, subject to advance appropriations limitations. Section 101(c) prescribes an apportionment methodology under 49 U.S.C. 47114–47117: apportionments are first calculated on an annualized $3,350,000,000 basis, then reduced by 39 percent. Sections 101(d)–(e) extend project grant authority (47104(c)) and the special apportionment rule (47114(c)(1)(J)) to May 10, 2024.

Section 102 extends numerous expiring authorities to May 10 or May 11, 2024, including war-risk insurance (44310(b)), UAS test ranges (44803(h)), special UAS authority (44807(d)), airspace hazard mitigation (44810(h)), and various pilot programs and advisory committees under the Vision 100 Act, the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012, the FAA Extension, Safety, and Security Act of 2016, and the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018. It sets revised interim authorization amounts for supplemental discretionary funds (47115(j)(4)(A): $340,321,762) and weather reporting programs (48105: $23,762,295).

Sections 103–105 revise interim authorizations: FAA operations under 49 U.S.C. 106(k) ($7,259,685,792); facilities and equipment under 48101(a) ($1,794,357,923); and research, engineering, and development under 48102(a) ($155,368,852), each for the period ending May 10, 2024. Section 106 raises Essential Air Service authorization (41742(a)(2)) to $216,192,407 and airports-not-receiving-sufficient-service funding (41743(e)(2)) to $6,092,896.

Title II extends Trust Fund financing. Section 201 amends I.R.C. § 9502(d)(1) and (e)(2) to extend expenditure authority to May 11, 2024, adding this Act to the enumerated authorizing statutes. Section 202 extends the aviation excise taxes funding the Trust Fund—fuel taxes (§ 4081(d)(2)(B)), ticket taxes on persons and property (§§ 4261(k), 4271(d)), and fractional-ownership-program provisions (§§ 4043(d), 4083(b), 4261(j))—to May 10 or May 11, 2024.

Title III, Section 301, extends counter-UAS authorities under section 210G(i) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 124n(i)) to May 11, 2024.

These provisions constitute authorizations, not appropriations.
